definition: A design principle that keeps related responsibilities together so a module or class changes for only one reason and has focused purpose.
ruleOfThumb: Group behaviour that changes for the same reason into the same unit; prefer small focused modules over broad multipurpose ones.

questions.prompt: Look at this service. Which observation best indicates a cohesion problem in the class?

options.text: This class groups many unrelated responsibilities into one unit and depends on several distinct external concerns.
options.explanation: The class mixes presentation rendering, business rules, and infra access. That indicates a module that will need changes for multiple unrelated reasons and is fragile. Keeping responsibilities focused reduces blast radius for changes and clarifies ownership.

options.text: This class primarily manipulates the same private fields across methods and keeps related behavior closely together.
options.explanation: When methods operate on the same private state and express closely related behavior, that is a sign of good cohesion, not poor cohesion. The presented code shows distinct responsibilities rather than just one shared state.

options.text: This class delegates core operations to small collaborators and exposes a unified, focused public interface for use.
options.explanation: Delegation to collaborators with a focused public API is usually desirable because it keeps responsibilities localized. This option describes a well-factored design and therefore is not the correct diagnosis for the sample.

options.text: This class is a thin wrapper around an external library and only translates types for a single concern.
options.explanation: A thin adapter that translates between layers for a single concern is typically acceptable and indicates focused responsibility. The sample code shows multiple distinct concerns rather than a single adapter role.

questions.prompt: Given this order processing module, which maintenance problem is most likely to occur if traffic and feature requests increase?

options.text: This module mixes multiple business responsibilities so modifying one rule will require changes across many unrelated functions.
options.explanation: Mixing validation, persistence, notification, and rendering in one module means a change to a business rule may force edits across unrelated functions. That increases coupling and regression risk as features evolve.

options.text: This module uses many small focused helpers which make the execution flow harder to trace and increase mental overhead.
options.explanation: Many small helpers can make tracing harder, but the presented code shows broad responsibilities in a single place rather than fragmentation by excessive tiny helpers. The primary maintenance risk is responsibility mixing.

options.text: This module relies on global mutable state that will cause unpredictable behavior as concurrency or parallel requests increase.
options.explanation: Global mutable state is indeed a serious concern, but the snippet shows sequential operations within a module. The immediate problem is that unrelated concerns are combined in one module, not evident global state usage.

options.text: This module depends on fragile exception routing that will frequently hide errors and make debugging and tracing difficult.
options.explanation: Fragile exception handling can hide errors, but the snippet does not demonstrate complex exception routing. The most likely maintainability issue here is the co-location of diverse concerns in one module.

questions.prompt: Compare Version A and Version B. Which version better supports easier maintenance and clearer ownership?

options.text: Version A groups validation persistence notification and rendering into a single service creating brittle interdependencies.
options.explanation: Version A centralizes many responsibilities inside one class, so changes in one area will ripple and require touching unrelated code. That increases regression scope and reduces testability and clear ownership.

options.text: Version B splits concerns into focused services with narrow responsibilities and composes them through a small coordinating facade.
options.explanation: Version B separates validation persistence and notification into distinct components and composes them via a facade. This reduces the blast radius of changes, clarifies ownership, and improves testability. This follows component cohesion guidance in Clean Architecture and SOLID composition recommendations.
